recipe_inventory.label: Fan et al. (2006): n-Dodecanethiol-capped gold nanocrystal preparation

source_locators.locator: Main PDF p. 4–5, Experimental, Synthesis of Gold NCs

recipe_inventory.scope: Quantified upstream Au preparation; film-feed ca.3nm and~7% width preserve source-level scope.
gaps: Complete five-page main, Scheme 1, Figures 1–3 and all 46 numbered references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed.
HAuCl4 hydration, reagent purities, aqueous phase-transfer duration, reduction temperature and numeric addition rate are not reported. The visible phase-transfer color endpoint is explicit.

The source gives TEOS (0.08 g) or BTEE without an independently stated BTEE amount. BTEE charge remains unknown; its two aging observations are retained as supporting routes rather than complete direct recipes.
HCl is 0.07 N or 1 N, 0.05 mL. The choice is not assigned to each film/aging specimen; no extra factorial experiments or inferred molar concentrations are created.
Quick-heating temperature/time for chloroform removal, NC stock concentration after clarification, spin duration, substrate cleaning and precise spin rate per specimen are unknown.
The 1 h room-temperature mixing precedes separately reported 0/5/24 h aging. No-aging means no additional aging, not absence of the 1 h sol–gel mixing.

Low-angle fcc parameters around 10.5/10.8 nm and Fm3m describe the nanocrystal superlattice mesostructure, not the atomic Au unit cell. No atomic coordinates or atomic Au lattice constant are supplied.
Representative TEM/optical/film-thickness results lack an exact aging/spin-rate/acid-strength crosswalk. They are supporting specimen contexts, not copied into each aging experiment.
Casting up to25 µm and micromolded stripe/dot patterns are supporting contexts: complete casting/micromolding schedules are not supplied. Cited methods remain unreviewed.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.

source_notes.label: Sol–gel rate and ordering
source_notes.summary: The authors connect acid-controlled silica condensation with film homogeneity. Extensive TEOS aging reduces ordering; BTEE aging has a weaker effect attributed to slower hydrolysis/condensation. This is source interpretation, not a quantitative rate model.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–4, Sol–gel and aging discussion

source_notes.label: Two structural length scales
source_notes.summary: Fcc and Fm3m in the low-angle/TEM discussion concern the nanocrystal superlattice. The10.5/10.8nm values must not be used as atomic Au lattice constants. No atomic coordinates are supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–4, XRD/TEM and orientation discussion

source_notes.label: Micelle-mediated compatibility
source_notes.summary: The source attributes aqueous stability to n-DT/CTAB chain interdigitation and assembly to charge/hydrogen-bond interactions with hydrolyzed silica. These are authors’ mechanisms, not direct surface-coordinate measurements.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Micelles and assembly interpretation

source_notes.label: Unresolved variants
source_notes.summary: Two acid strengths are listed without sample assignment. BTEE has no separately stated charge. Representative optical/TEM/film-thickness observations remain separate from exact aging labels.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–5, Methods and figure captions
